subsystems.name: Display
subsystems.role: creates the image that is projected onto the retina.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: supplies electricity without wires or bulky batteries.

subsystems.name: Control and communication
subsystems.role: receives data from an external device and drives the display.

subsystems.name: Optics and eye tracking
subsystems.role: directs light to the retina and senses eye movement for stable images.

subsystems.name: Biocompatible encapsulation
subsystems.role: keeps electronics safe from tears and the eye safe from materials.

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: prevents heat buildup on the eye.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical path
buildSteps.detail: Simulate how a tiny display's light can be focused onto the retina without distorting the wearer's normal vision.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the micro-display
buildSteps.detail: Grow micro-LEDs on a substrate, then transfer them to a flexible, transparent carrier using pick-and-place techniques.

buildSteps.title: Integrate electronics
buildSteps.detail: Deposit transparent conductors and antennas, and bond driver chips onto the flexible circuit.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate in lens
buildSteps.detail: Cast the electronics in a biocompatible hydrogel, ensuring oxygen permeability and a smooth surface.

buildSteps.title: Add wireless power and communication
buildSteps.detail: Embed coils or antennas for inductive power and data transfer, then seal them.

buildSteps.title: Test in vitro
buildSteps.detail: Soak lenses in artificial tears to check for leakage, corrosion and leaching of materials.

buildSteps.title: Test in vivo
buildSteps.detail: Place prototypes on animal or human eyes in controlled studies to measure comfort, safety and image quality.

prerequisites.why: micro-LEDs exist on rigid panels; making them transparent and flexible on a curved lens is not yet routine.

prerequisites.tech: Wireless power transfer for ocular implants
prerequisites.why: inductive power is used in some medical implants, but miniaturising it for a contact lens while limiting heat is difficult.
the eye is sensitive; materials must not leach and must block tears while allowing oxygen to the cornea.

prerequisites.tech: High-resolution optics on a curved surface
prerequisites.why: projecting a sharp image onto the retina from a lens that moves with the eye requires novel optical designs.
Bluetooth and similar standards can handle the data rates, but custom low-power chips are needed for integration.

pathway.milestone: lab prototypes demonstrate single-colour images on a contact lens, powered wirelessly
pathway.unlocks: proof that the concept is feasible.

pathway.milestone: full-colour, higher-resolution displays with eye tracking in animal studies
clinical trials for medical uses, such as restoring sight or treating eye disease
pathway.unlocks: regulatory approval for limited medical applications.

pathway.milestone: consumer AR contact lenses with all-day wear
pathway.unlocks: hands-free augmented reality for everyday use.
